metadata.title: This Week: What Shipped, What's Next
metadata.register: Conversational-Balanced, first-person, honest and straightforward — not the house Teardown/am_onyx register cli-explainer defaults to. Matches the af_bella / @HumanitariansAI precedent set on this user's other reels.
metadata.note: User asked for a 'CLI Explainer' by name. Built on the cli-explainer skill's REQUIRED story spine (B00 cold open -> PROBLEM -> ASK -> CODE -> OUTPUT -> CHANGE -> CODE -> OUTPUT -> SUMMARY -> NEXT STEPS -> OUTRO, real code shown via ClaudeCodeBeat, one required revision cycle) but with two disclosed substitutions: (1) voice/branding — af_bella + @HumanitariansAI instead of the skill's default Teardown/am_onyx/@NikBearBrown, per explicit user request for a woman's voice and matching this user's other two reels; (2) render pipeline — the skill's documented `vox_run.sh`/`vox_compile.py`/`type_check.py` do not exist in this toolkit install (verified: not found anywhere under runtime/scripts or runtime/qc); rendered instead through the same run.sh/compile.py/static_scene_check.py/manim_layout_audit.py/final_frame_check.py pipeline used successfully on this user's other three reels this session. The CLI loop's 'build' is real: weekly_recap_v1.py and weekly_recap_v2.py are genuine Python scripts, both actually run (not invented) to capture the CODE/OUTPUT beats' real source and output. v1 is a flat, undifferentiated list of the week's three items; v2 splits them into DONE THIS WEEK vs STARTING NEXT WEEK -- a real structural revision, not a cosmetic one, which doubles as the user's own stated concern (their revision-prompt template #5 asked for exactly this separation) already resolved in the initial cut.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — ask shown answered; opens with the host's self-introduction, per cli-explainer's own reference-example convention (persona name + tagline directly in B00)
beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Agrima. Let's skip the highlight reel — here's the actual log of what I did this week, and what's starting next.

props.command: claude "help me build a real log of what I actually did this week"
props.segment: This Week: What Shipped, What's Next

beats.role_note: the problem, the context, the stakes — BEFORE the CLI loop
beats.narration_text: Most weekly updates are a highlight reel — the wins, dressed up. I wanted something closer to a real log: what actually got done, kept separate from what's just getting started.
beats.visual_intent: title card: 'a real log, not a highlight reel' — no composer yet

beats.narration_text: Start simple: ask Claude for a script that just logs the week — the article, the Brutalist workflow, the fashion project kickoff — one flat list, nothing fancy yet.

props.command:
claude "write weekly_recap_v1.py -- log this week:
  the article, the video tool, what's next"
props.segment: This Week: What Shipped, What's Next

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL generated code, trimmed to what teaches; weekly_recap_v1.py was really run
beats.narration_text: Here's what it wrote — a flat list, three entries, no ranking, no spin. Just: published this, learned this, met about this.

props.title: weekly_recap_v1.py

beats.role_note: OPEN vox slot -> Manim video; the real weekly_recap_v1.py output, visualized as three same-weight cards
beats.narration_text: Run it, and here's the week: the resume piece, out on Substack. The Brutalist workflow, actually learned — not just installed. And a first meeting on the fashion project. All three, same weight, no sense of what's finished and what's just beginning.
beats.visual_intent: Manim: three cards in a flat row — a mock Substack article header, a video-production icon card labeled 16:9 + 9:16, a calendar/next-meeting card — all the same visual weight, undifferentiated

beats.narration_text: That's the problem, though — a flat list treats 'I published this' the same as 'we had one meeting about this.' So: revise it. Split what's actually finished from what's just starting.

props.command:
claude "update weekly_recap_v1.py -> weekly_recap_v2.py:
  -> split into DONE THIS WEEK vs STARTING NEXT WEEK"
props.segment: This Week: What Shipped, What's Next

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the revised code; weekly_recap_v2.py was really run
beats.narration_text: Same week, same three items — now in two lists. Done: the article, the workflow. Next: the fashion project, which starts for real next week.

props.title: weekly_recap_v2.py
props.code:
DONE = [
    {"item": "Published 'The Death of the Generic Resume'", "where": "Substack"},
    {"item": "Learned the Brutalist workflow (16:9 + 9:16)", "where": "brutalist.art"},
]

NEXT = [
    {"item": "Fashion sustainability: forecasting, sampling,
              traceability", "where": "starts next week"},
]

def log():
    print("DONE THIS WEEK")
    ...
    print("STARTING NEXT WEEK")
    ...

beats.role_note: OPEN vox slot -> Manim video; the real weekly_recap_v2.py output, visualized as a DONE/NEXT split
beats.narration_text: Re-run it, and the shape changes completely. Done this week: the piece is published, the workflow's actually mine now. Starting next week: the fashion sustainability work — forecasting, sampling, material traceability. Nothing here is finished yet. That's the point of saying so.
beats.visual_intent: Manim: the same three cards, now regrouped under two headers — DONE THIS WEEK (checkmark, good-green) holding the Substack + Brutalist cards; STARTING NEXT WEEK (arrow, terracotta) holding the fashion card — a vertical divider between the two groups

beats.narration_text: So that's the real log: one piece shipped, one skill genuinely learned, and one project just getting its first real push. Separating done from next isn't a small detail — it's the difference between a recap and a highlight reel.
beats.visual_intent: recap card: 'done' vs 'next' reframed as the actual lesson, not just a formatting choice

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in, viewer-addressed, read aloud and discussed
beats.narration_text: Your turn — same prompt, your week. Ask Claude for your own recap script, split the same way: done, and starting. It's a small habit, but it keeps you honest about what actually happened versus what you just started thinking about.

props.command:
claude "write me a weekly_recap.py that logs my actual
  week, split into what's done and what's just starting"
props.segment: This Week: What Shipped, What's Next

beats.role_note: OUTRO LAW — restate the episode title, last beat
beats.narration_text: This week: what shipped, what's next. Logged for real, not hyped up.
